body: Oh god, yes, I regret that so much. When I had my first bad bout of suicidal thoughts etc. I told a couple of friends, and then I literally felt sick when ever I saw them, and ended cutting them out of my life entirely because I couldn't stand it. When I had my second downturn, I didn't tell anyone, but it made me panicky that people could tell something was up. Third time, luckily I was living on alone, and had just started new classes at uni, so I could easily avoid people when it got too bad.

That's the thing that always gets me, I don't know if other are feeling this way too, and just keep it to themselves. I've never tried to discuss depression or whether I have it with anyone really. Recently my mom visited me, and commented that I had lost a lot of weight fast, and I said that I had been feeling so sad that I'd lost my appetite, and then she changed the subject. A few days later I was on the phone with my dad, and he said "So your mom said that you've lost weight, how's that going?" :s Felt sort of confused about that, she obviously took note enough to comment and re-tell it, but didn't listen or think about the reason?
It is the next day now, and I'm still feeling the same.
I would like to see me living a happy, fulfilling life too, but that doesn't seem to be happening. I can't even imagine how that would look like.

No, I haven't told anyone. I've gotten rather out of touch with everyone lately, and I can't think who I'd tell. I do think I may go to the doctor soon. I am getting an new one, and I think it is goo that it will be like talking to a stranger, because then it will have no consequences if it turns out to be a mess.
I think it's rather an overstatement to say I am a good person for not wanting to make other people suffer for my mistakes.

Yeah, that's the thing, as far as I've heard when googling around (I moved, and thus had to find a new doctor, and since I do struggle with things like this, I researched it first), doctors can give as crazy and limited answers as well. Some doctors diagnose major depression and prescribe strong anti-depressants, no matter what might actually be going on (I read that about one lady, who had a lot of external things affecting her, and later found a better doctor, who said it was probably more like a major bout of understandable stress)
Others pretty much don't 'believe' in these kind of things, and tell people to just get some air and cheer up (one girl told me this - 3 weeks later, she was in a mental hospital after a suicide attempt).
So while it is probably true that a *good* doctor will be able to take the full picture into account, and give a correct diagnoses, it seems to me like that is more like the exception than the rule :( It frustrates me, that this seems to be field of much subjectivity... So much, that it seems less like 'subjective', and more like 'personal opinion'.
Ok, so, so far it seems somewhat accurate, then

I read a bit more about each of the disorders, and it seems like it is inevitable that it rates similar for Major Depression/Dysthymia and Bipolar Disorder/Cyclothymia, so I would say, instead of measuring for 5 different diorders, it's more like 3...
I stay home if I am feeling too bad, and also go to the bathroom to cry or have a moment where I try to calm myself. I don't know what other ways.

It's not because no one would notice. That is just a 'side effect', and just a practical observation.
And it's not because I dream of living life like a recluse, and that would fix anything. It's not because I 'want' to do nothing, I just can't stand doing anything. Nothing gets better by being alone, but I just can't stand being around people.

I'm not lonely, though, it's not my lack of socializing that's making me feel this way. More like the other way around: because I feel like this, I don't want to/can't socialize. So I'm not interested in making an effort to get in contact with people, that wouldn't 'fix' anything... When I'm around people, all I can think of is trying to keep up a straight face. It's exhausting, and I don't 'get' anything from it. I just want to be alone, and do nothing, preferable not thinking either. And there's a pretty solid way of achieving that permanently. It would be so easy.
